title: #3: Facebook Ads Basics For Life Coaches - victoriagibson.com

facts.fact: The page states the average Facebook user clicks on 12 ads a month.
facts.quote: The average Facebook user clicks on 12 ads a month, and there are 2.7 billion daily users

facts.fact: The author says a Facebook ad budget can be as little as $5 a day for growing email subscribers with a freebie ad.
facts.quote: it can be as little as $5 a day!

facts.fact: The author reports that a client, Hayley, obtained 15 six-month coaching clients from her free Facebook group alone using Facebook ads.
facts.quote: Hayley was able to get 15 x 6-month coaching clients from her free group alone.

facts.fact: The author states the author has been running Facebook Ads for herself and coaching clients for a decade.
facts.quote: I’ve been running Facebook Ads for myself and my coaching clients for a decade now

facts.fact: The author recommends life coaches use four types of Facebook ads: engagement, lead, video, and messaging ads.
facts.quote: There are only 4 different types of ads I would recommend you use as a life coach

facts.fact: The author states that Facebook lead ads can be used even without a website, with Facebook collecting email addresses for the advertiser.
facts.quote: you can get started with a single ad, even if you don’t have a website and Facebook will collect email addresses for you.

facts.fact: The author claims video ads are the Facebook ads that get clicked on the most.
facts.quote: The Facebook Ads that get clicked on the most are video ads.

facts.fact: Facebook Ads organizes ads into three levels: Campaign, Ad Set, and Ads.
facts.quote: Facebook Ads break your ads down into three levels – Campaign, Ad Set and Ads.

facts.fact: At the Campaign level, the author says advertisers only need to choose between two objectives, Traffic or Engagement, when starting with simple ads.
facts.quote: At the Campaign level, you will get to choose your objective, and you only need to worry about two.

facts.fact: The author recommends a starting budget of $20 per day for each ad set.
facts.quote: So rather than start high, start with $20 a day for each ad set and scale up 10% of that budget a day as long as your ads hold firm.

facts.fact: The author recommends increasing an ad set's daily budget by 10% per day as long as the ads perform well.
facts.quote: start with $20 a day for each ad set and scale up 10% of that budget a day as long as your ads hold firm.

facts.fact: The author advises watching Cost Per Click and says to be concerned if CPC creeps above $2.
facts.quote: Keep an eye on your Cost Per Click (CPC), especially if it creeps above $2

facts.fact: The author states that Click Through Rate should sit above 1.5% at least for ads.
facts.quote: your Click Through Rate (CTR) should sit above 1.5% at least.

facts.fact: The author says they have run Facebook ads for a decade.
facts.quote: Having run Facebook ads for a decade, I’ve seen many coaches use Facebook Ads with amazing success.

facts.fact: The author reports that Facebook ads have produced $3,000 coaching clients from scratch, $7,000 mastermind clients, and $497 workshop sales for coaches they have seen.
facts.quote: Think $3,000 coaching clients from scratch, $7,000 mastermind clients and $497 workshop sales which have really just been the tip of the iceberg.

facts.fact: The author advises against sending ads directly to a coaching payment page when people likely have not yet heard of the advertiser.
facts.quote: It’s not recommended to send ads directly to a payment page for your coaching if it’s likely those clicking on your ad haven’t yet heard of you.

facts.fact: Facebook allows ad targeting by demographics such as age, education, and family status, as well as likes, interests, and behaviours.
facts.quote: Not only can you target your audience based on demographics like age, education and family status, but you can also target who your ads are shown to based on their likes, interests and behaviours.

facts.fact: The author describes a landing page as a page created for lead capture that focuses on one simple action, such as entering an email or registering for a webinar.
facts.quote: A landing page is a specific page you create for the purposes of lead capture, and it’s simpler than a website and focused on your audience taking just one simple action
